title: chemoqbit: reaction energetics on qubits, from molecular integrals to the instruction stream of an FPGA state-vector simulator
description:
Code, results and tests for end-to-end studies of chemical reactions on qubits, from molecular integrals to the 32-bit instruction stream a hardware state-vector simulator executes.

Circuits and electronic structure: PySCF active spaces from CCSD natural orbitals, optionally embedded in point charges, mapped to qubits by Jordan-Wigner; UCCSD-VQE and fermionic ADAPT-VQE with analytic adjoint gradients; compilation to Pauli exponentials, a peephole optimiser, a 32-bit instruction set, and bit-accurate 18-bit fixed-point emulation of the qsim-pynq FPGA datapath (PYNQ-Z2). Every circuit energy is checked against exact diagonalisation in the same space.

Reaction energetics: transition-state theory rates, Wigner and Eckart tunnelling, and composite levels combining CCSD(T) with the circuit result in the same active space.

Applications. Proton-transfer tautomerism of formamide and 5-fluorouracil. Hydride transfer in thymidylate synthase from a 96-atom active-site cluster built from PDB 1TLS, with a GFN2-xTB reaction scan, a frozen-atom-aware P-RFO saddle search, finite-difference Hessians, H/D/T kinetic isotope effects, DFT single points and ONIOM layering. A lattice protein-folding benchmark on the diamond lattice with Miyazawa-Jernigan contact energies and the dense turn encoding.

New in 1.2.0. Prolyl cis/trans isomerisation of capped Xaa-Pro dipeptides, including the phosphorylation effect. Ligand-binding pocket clusters cut from crystal structures with in-silico alanine truncation, applied to CFTR with lumacaftor and acetylcholinesterase with donepezil. Amyloid steric-zipper interfaces as cluster models, for tau, alpha-synuclein and SOD1 segments, benchmarked against deposited structures. A six-system chalcogen S_N2 ladder separating nucleophile from electrophile effects in thiol-disulfide and selenium-sulfur exchange, with its numerical precision floor measured from closed thermodynamic constraints rather than asserted. Shrake-Rupley solvent accessibility, and geometric feasibility analyses of the buried Cys57-Cys146 disulfide of SOD1: solvent accessibility, backside attack geometry, side-chain rotamer scans and the displacement required to open the attack site. These are geometric and semiempirical analyses, not completed energetic determinations.

New in 1.3.0. A reproducible epitope map for conformation-specific antibodies against misfolded SOD1: per-residue Shrake-Rupley accessibility of the native holo dimer against the middle layer of a three-layer stack of the wild-type fibril, which is the difference such an antibody needs, since an epitope exposed on both states binds normal protein in every cell that makes SOD1. Eleven residues are buried natively and exposed on the aggregate. The published rationale of a recent conformation-specific antibody is tested against it. A residue-accessibility bound catches summed alternate conformers and colliding residue numbers. Crystal structures for this work are fetched from RCSB like the rest. Also packaged in this release, and absent from 1.2.0: the FastAPI service is now actually installed by the package, which it was not, and the continuous integration fixes that followed.

New in 1.4.0. The SOD1 geometric analyses of 1.2.0 are completed and replicated, and the energetic determination they were waiting for is here. The attack geometry is measured across three crystal forms rather than one -- 2C9U at 1.24 A, 1HL5 at 1.80 A and 7FB9 at 2.70 A -- keeping every (chain, altloc) as its own set of atoms rather than resolving alternate conformers by occupancy, which gives thirty-seven chains, thirty-four of them modelling a formed disulfide. The backside attack angle at Cys146 spans 131.9 to 146.8 degrees and reaches the 150-degree collinearity floor in none of them; the attack site 3.3 A beyond the sulfur is occupied in all thirty-seven, with main-chain atoms among the occupants in all thirty-seven. The identity of the occupying residues does not replicate -- two of them in a single chain each, against Cys146 in all thirty-seven and Gly147 in thirty-six -- which is the result that matters for what can be claimed: the obstruction is the main chain of the neighbouring strands and not any named side chain, so no rotamer rearrangement removes it. All four intramolecular routes any free SOD1 cysteine could take to the disulfide are measured, not only the one the literature names, which closes the relay objection: SOD1 has four cysteines, two of them are the bond, and there is no spare thiol to resolve an intermediate.

The conformational work is now determined and not pending. Bringing Cys6 to 3.12 A of Cys146 at a 175-degree approach, in a 259-atom cluster with the outer shell held and the local backbone free, costs +131.02 kcal/mol at GFN2-xTB with ALPB solvation. Inverting Eyring at 310.15 K with the full k_B.T/h prefactor allows 25.18, 28.82 and 31.23 kcal/mol for one event per day, per year and per fifty years, so the approach alone exceeds the fifty-year ceiling by a factor of 4.2 before any bond-forming barrier is added, and crosses it at about 6.5 A with 3.3 A still to travel. Every covalent bond of that series was measured at every scan point against the relaxed reference: none is stretched by more than 11 per cent, and that one is the attacked disulfide lengthening from 2.02 to 2.24 A as the nucleophile closes.

No complementary upper bound is reported, and the reason is recorded rather than omitted. Held rigid, the fold does not yield elastically to contact: it breaks a covalent bond. Restraining the backbone alone ruptured the Cys57-Cys146 disulfide between 6.27 and 5.92 A, with the nucleophile still 5.9 A away and taking no part in it. Restraining that bond at its relaxed length as well moved the failure instead of removing it, to the Cys57 CB-SG bond at the same step. Both runs are archived in results/ with the diagnosis that retires them, because each added restraint relocates the rupture and a constraint set chosen until the curve behaves is chosen for its effect on the result. What the two agree on is reported: a rigid fold cannot be pushed past 5.9 A, and arrives there having spent 2.7 times the fifty-year ceiling on strain alone.

Validation gains the check that would have caught the above at the first bad point rather than eleven hours later. covalent_stretch is the longest covalent bond of a restrained geometry over its length in the relaxed reference, with the bond list built once from that reference so a broken bond cannot be re-derived as simply absent; it is fatal, and replayed over the three runs it passes the reported series and stops both discarded ones at their first ruptured point. Long scans now checkpoint per point and resume from the last one, rather than holding a stage in memory until it ends. A correction: the epitope map named a residue as occluding the attack trajectory which occludes nothing, absent from every occupancy list at both probe radii and from all thirty-seven chains; the claim is corrected in place and dated, and no computed value changed.

Validation. A physical-bounds module carrying 37 checks, each with the reason it exists written into the code; an auditor that recomputes them from stored geometry and separates recorded dead ends from open faults; a stall detector deriving its unit list from systemd; and a 101-case self-test that exercises every bound in both directions, using archived real failures as labelled positives. Long runs are resumable systemd units with atomic checkpoints and per-point resume.

A FastAPI module serves the cases and their instruction streams. A Dockerfile pins the exact versions the results were produced with. Crystal structures are fetched from RCSB rather than redistributed. Educational; not for clinical use.

New in 1.4.1. The derivation behind the TDP-43 charge-step result is deposited rather than only its numbers: scripts/tdp43_charge_steps.py converts the published conversion percentages of a charge-variant series to rate constants and reports the multiple each step of motif net charge buys, under both the binned-observation and the authors' fitted-line conventions, because the first step depends on which is used while the ordering does not. It reads its constructs from tdp43_frailty.py rather than carrying a second copy. Writing it corrected a number: the conversion hazard had been described as flat to 4 per cent across a four-fold range of time, which is the coefficient of variation of the three estimates, but read as a bound on any one estimate it understates by more than a factor of two, the worst point being 6.0 per cent from the mean and lowest to highest 10.1 per cent. All three measures are now reported so that a sentence quoting one cannot be read as another.

The SOD1 attack-site replication is also recorded at the second probe distance: the cross-crystal analysis defines the ideal attack point 3.0 A beyond the leaving sulfur in the methods and computed it at 3.3 A, so both were run and both are archived. Nothing the exclusion rests on moves -- thirty-seven chains, thirty-four with a formed disulfide, the site occupied in all thirty-seven with main-chain atoms among the occupants in all thirty-seven, no chain reaching the 150-degree floor -- while the identity of the occupying residues does move, which is the quantity already reported as not replicating.

Tooling: the Markdown-to-PDF renderer draws the thirteen characters outside Latin-1 that the built-in PDF fonts cannot, which had been emitting filled squares where the manuscripts write Greek, reaction arrows and angle brackets, and it now reports what it had to borrow. A sibling renders the same Markdown subset to .docx. CITATION.cff, which still read 1.3.0 in the 1.4.0 release, is corrected.
